content.text: The licence grant meets our preferred position on every parameter, so no redline is needed.

input.quote: 13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.
input.rationale: Section 13 satisfies every element of the preferred position. Clause 13.1 grants the subscription access right to "Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf" on a worldwide, non-exclusive basis for internal business purposes, and extends to Authorized Users — so affiliates and contractors are expressly in scope with no need for the fallback notice mechanic. Clause 13.2 makes paid-up and Deliverable-embedded software a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence" to Customer and its Affiliates, including modification and derivative-work rights and contractor support. Clause 13.3 confirms transferability to an Affiliate or successor via Section 24, and limits revocation or suspension to a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a reasonable cure opportunity — i.e., no revocation at Vendor's discretion. Section 24.1 backs this up by allowing Customer to assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor without Vendor's consent, and 24.4 bars Vendor from terminating, repricing, or reducing service on a Customer change of control. The "Affiliate" definition (1.1) is a standard majority-control test that does not narrow the grant. The restrictions in 13.4 are ordinary anti-misuse covenants and are expressly carved back for authorized security testing and Customer Data and output, so they do not undercut the grant. No deviation from the licence-scope rule.
